tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

3. Translate it in **every** `lang/*.json` (19 files) in the same change — new, reworded or removed
   text alike. Keep the `{n}` placeholders, any leading/trailing space and a leading icon (`🤖 `,
   `■ `). `test.cmd` fails on a string missing from any file, on a translation whose English is gone
   from the code, on duplicate keys, empty values and on those three rules.
4. New built-in language: add it to `Loc.BuiltInLanguages` (code = .NET culture name, display name in
   that language), add `lang/<code>.json` with every key and an `<EmbeddedResource>` line in the
   csproj next to the others; the tests check the three agree. For a local fix or an extra language
   without a rebuild, drop the file in `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\lang` (it also
   overrides embedded entries).
5. Text set from code after the XAML is built does not follow a language switch on its own: make
   sure `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or the view's `RefreshLanguage()`) redoes it. A tool window that
   lives outside the panel subscribes to `Loc.LanguageChanged` itself (Code Changes, Claude Usage).
   A modeless window built in code is retranslated in place with `UI.LocTree.Retranslate(window)`
   from `RefreshChatLanguage()` (GitHub Issues). Modal dialogs and menus built when opened need nothing.

root = sys.argv[1]
for code, tr in T.items():
    p = os.path.join(root, "lang", code + ".json")
    d = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    assert len(tr) == 6, code
    items = list(d.items())
    for k, v in tr.items():
        if k in d:
            d[k] = v
            items = list(d.items())
            continue
        idx = next((i for i, (ek, _) in enumerate(items) if ek.lower() > k.lower()), len(items))
        items.insert(idx, (k, v))
        d = dict(items)
    out = json.dumps(dict(items), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2).replace("\n", "\r\n") + "\r\n"
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(out)
    print(code, "ok")

root = sys.argv[1]
for code, tr in T.items():
    p = os.path.join(root, "lang", code + ".json")
    d = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    assert len(tr) == 6, code
    items = list(d.items())
    for k, v in tr.items():
        if k in d:
            d[k] = v
            items = list(d.items())
            continue
        idx = next((i for i, (ek, _) in enumerate(items) if ek.lower() > k.lower()), len(items))
        items.insert(idx, (k, v))
        d = dict(items)
    out = json.dumps(dict(items), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2).replace("\n", "\r\n") + "\r\n"
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(out)
    print(code, "ok")

for code, tr in T.items():
    p = os.path.join(root, "lang", code + ".json")
    d = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    assert len(tr) == 6, code
    items = list(d.items())
    for k, v in tr.items():
        if k in d:
            d[k] = v
            items = list(d.items())
            continue
        idx = next((i for i, (ek, _) in enumerate(items) if ek.lower() > k.lower()), len(items))
        items.insert(idx, (k, v))
        d = dict(items)
    out = json.dumps(dict(items), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2).replace("\n", "\r\n") + "\r\n"
    open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(out)

content.content:
724:- Tool cards are one informative line when collapsed (`UI/ChatToolPresentation.cs`, pure and unit-tested in `Tests/ChatToolPresentationTests.cs`): `ChatToolPresenter.Describe(name, inputJson)` returns the icon, title, target (file / command / pattern), a badge (`+12 -3`, `lines 10-14`, `1/2`) and, for `Edit`/`MultiEdit`/`Write`/`NotebookEdit`, a diff built with DiffPlex from `old_string`/`new_string` (all lines added for `Write`). A column of bare "Read"/"Edit" labels said nothing about the turn. Capped at 400 diff rows with 2 lines of context; no line numbers, because the payload is a fragment and any number shown would be wrong. Unknown tools, MCP-prefixed names (`mcp__server__tool`) and renamed arguments must degrade to "name + raw JSON" rather than throw — the inventory changes with every CLI release. Shell tools (v276.0: `Bash`/`shell`/`PowerShell`/`run_command`/`execute`) show the command itself as the opened card's input, not the JSON payload where every quote and backslash came out escaped (`\"`), which read as an encoding error: `BuildToolCallMessage` takes `ChatToolPresenter.FormatShellInput` (command, then any argument other than the command and `description` as `name: value` lines) and falls back to the indented JSON (`FormatToolInput`) when it returns null. Failed calls open their card by themselves only while `ExpandFailedToolCalls` is on (default; `CompleteToolCallMessage*`) — Claude reports a chained command whose last part exits non-zero as a failed call even when the rest worked, and usually recovers by itself.
785:- Claude's permission/plan-mode switch is live too (issue #193, v241.0). Every composer pick (Plan mode, Skip permissions, Auto mode, Accept edits, Manual mode, Ask/Skip, and `/plan`) used to relaunch, which killed a turn still in flight. `ApplyNativePermissionSwitchAsync`/`ApplySessionPermissionSwitchAsync` now first send `{"subtype":"set_permission_mode","mode":…}` via `ClaudeStreamJsonSession.SetPermissionModeAsync` and relaunch only when that is not a confirmed success (non-Claude agent, dead process, old CLI). Measured against CLI 2.1.296: sent mid-turn it returns `success` at once, a `system/status` frame reports the new mode, and the turn runs on to its normal `result`; every transition among `acceptEdits`/`auto`/`plan`/`manual`/`bypassPermissions` succeeds both from a `--dangerously-skip-permissions` launch and from a `--permission-mode … --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` one (the CLI answers `manual` with mode `default`; an unknown mode is `invalid_mode`). `ClaudeCommandBuilder.ToLivePermissionMode` maps Skip permissions to `bypassPermissions`, since live it is a mode rather than the launch flag. The settings are saved before the switch, so a later relaunch (model fallback, agent restart) launches with the same mode; `SetPermissionModeAsync` also writes the mode into the session's own launch options, because the interrupt-recovery relaunch in `OnHostExited` launches from those and Stop would otherwise put the session back in its launch mode (while an interrupt is pending it only updates the options and skips the request to the exiting process). Leaving plan mode mid-turn is deliberately *not* live: tested in VS, the agent read the switch as "planning is over" and began writing files from a plan nobody approved. `ClaudeCommandBuilder.ShouldWaitForPlanToEnd` (turn in flight and the CLI-reported mode is `plan`, target not Plan mode) defers it: the pick goes into `ClaudeStreamJsonSession.PendingPlanExitMode`, which the parser's `PlanExitModeProvider` attaches to the next plain plan approval as `updatedPermissions:[{type:setMode,mode,destination:session}]` (measured on 2.1.296 with `acceptEdits` and `auto`: the CLI applies it in the same step, `system/status` confirms it); "Approve and skip permissions" still wins over it. If no approval carries it, `ApplyDeferredNativePermissionSwitch`/`ApplyDeferredSessionPermissionSwitch` apply it from the turn-completed handlers, only if the agent session is still the one the pick was made for. The live mode itself is `ClaudeStreamJsonSession.PermissionMode`, fed by the parser's `PermissionModeReported` from every `system/init` and `system/status` frame (a plain plan approval reports `default`; so does `manual`). Entering plan mode mid-turn stays immediate — that is what the issue asked for.
790:- Plan mode is a launch flag, so toggling it relaunches (resumed, so the conversation so far becomes the plan's input). lines: - The permission selector is five-way (v188.0, expanded v189.0): Plan mode / Skip permissions / Auto mode / Accept edits / Manual mode. Before v188.0 the extension always forced `--permission-mode acceptEdits` (or `plan`, or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`) on every native-mode launch, so the CLI's own `--permission-mode auto` (verified present on CLI 2.1.278: `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `bypassPermissions`, `manual`, `dontAsk`, `plan`) was unreachable from the composer. v189.0 renamed "Auto" to "Auto mode" and "Ask permission" to "Accept edits" (both a truthful rename only — "Accept edits" is still the same `acceptEdits` launch under the hood, not a new code path) and added a genuinely new "Manual mode", which launches `--permission-mode manual` — the CLI's real "ask before every tool call", with no standing allow even for file edits, which is what tells it apart from "Accept edits". A launch still always carries an explicit mode, so this makes `auto` and `manual` selectable — it does **not** defer to the user's `permissions.defaultMode` in their Claude settings.json; deferring would need a further choice that sends no `--permission-mode` at all. `ClaudeAutoPermissions`/`ClaudeManualMode` (`Settings`) / `AutoPermissions`/`ManualMode` (`NativeChatSessionState`) are two more bools alongside `ClaudePlanMode`/`PlanMode` and `ClaudeDangerouslySkipPermissions`/`SkipPermissions`; every selection handler that turns one on clears the other three. "Accept edits", "Auto mode" and "Manual mode" only differ in which CLI mode they launch with — neither is a distinct C# code path beyond the flag itself. The plan-only, session-history and terminal (classic embedded terminal) code paths are untouched; this is native mode only (terminal mode honors only plan mode, see above).

- Four flags, one resolver (v188.0, extended v189.0): `ClaudeCommandBuilder.ResolvePermissionChoice(plan, skip, auto, manual)` -> `ClaudePermissionChoice`, plus `ToPermissionMode` for the flag value; both unit-tested in `AgentStreamParsingTests`. `CreateClaudeSession`, `GetChatPermissionLabel` (both overloads) and `BuildChatPermissionMenu` (both overloads) all go through it instead of testing the four flags in their own order, because they did not agree: the launch resolved skip before auto while the caption resolved auto before skip, so a session holding both flags launched `--dangerously-skip-permissions` under an "Auto" caption — the display naming the *safer* of the two modes. The menus now check `choice == X` per entry, so exactly one entry can ever be checked. Precedence is plan > skip > auto > manual > accept edits (the default), the order the launch flags already used extended one step further for manual.

- What made the flags contradict each other (v188.0): only something setting one without clearing the others. The 🤖 provider menu's "Claude Code: Skip Permissions" did exactly that — it predates native mode but is visible there too — so it now clears plan, auto and manual and refreshes the composer caption. `OnChatAutoPermissionsSelected`/`OnChatManualModeSelected` also compare against the whole target state instead of their own flag; bailing out on `ClaudeAutoPermissions` (or `ClaudeManualMode`) alone no-opped while a stale skip flag was the one being launched, which is the #150 trap "Accept edits" (`OnChatAcceptEditsSelected`, formerly `OnChatAskPermissionSelected`) documents.

Measured against CLI 2.1.273: a live `{"subtype":"set_permission_mode","mode":"bypassPermissions"}` is refused ("session was not launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions") unless the process was launched with `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`, so `ClaudeCommandBuilder` now adds that flag to every non-skip launch (it makes bypass available, not active). The plan card's own "Approve and skip permissions" button (Tag `skip`, shown only when `CanApproveAndSkipPermissions`; the ▾ menu only holds the model entries) then answers the `ExitPlanMode` `can_use_tool` with `behavior:allow` plus `updatedPermissions:[{type:setMode,mode:bypassPermissions,destination:session}]` (`AgentInteractionRequest.AllowAndSkipPermissions` -> `SkipPermissionsRequested`, read by `ClaudeStreamParser`'s responder); the session's `OnApproveAndSkipPermissions` callback also sets its own `_options.DangerouslySkipPermissions` so an interrupt-recovery relaunch stays in bypass. `OnChatInteractionResolved` then mirrors the choice into the composer as the conversation-only `PlanExitChoice` override (v212.0, #181 — was the saved `ClaudeDangerouslySkipPermissions`/`SkipPermissions`) without a relaunch. A plain "Approve" out of an extension-chosen Plan mode carries `setMode acceptEdits` the same way (v314.0, #210 follow-up): `ClaudeCommandBuilder.ResolvePlanApprovalMode` (via `PlanExitModeProvider`) returns the #193 pending pick if any, else `acceptEdits` when the session's own launch options say `plan` and not bypass, else null. Measured on CLI 2.1.328: an allow without a mode returns the CLI to its pre-plan mode, which for a session launched in plan is `default` — every later edit asked while the selector read Accept edits. A plan the agent entered on its own (EnterPlanMode from another mode) is left to the CLI, which returns to that mode. Either approved mode is for that plan only (v257.0 for skip, v314.0 for Accept edits, issue #210): approving arms `_nativePlanRestorePending`/`_nativePlanRestoreChoice`/`_nativePlanRestoreFrom` (tabs: `PlanRestorePending`/`PlanRestoreChoice`/`PlanRestoreFrom`) with the override's previous value and the approved one, and the turn-completed handler (`RestoreNativeModeAfterApprovedPlan`/`RestoreSessionModeAfterApprovedPlan`) puts it back and applies it through `ApplyNativePermissionSwitchAsync` (live `set_permission_mode`, relaunch fallback) — so a conversation that was in Plan mode plans again on the next prompt. content.text:
All three suggestions from #268 are in version 316.0. It's committed and pushed to master as `777815c`, published to the Marketplace, and I replied on the issue and closed it. The unit tests pass (1104/1104), but I haven't tried any of this in a running Visual Studio, and nothing was tested against the live Claude CLI.

**What changed:**
1. **"Keep planning" with an empty feedback box:** the agent is now told to end its turn and wait for your next message. Before, it opened a question card asking what to change. Typing feedback before clicking still makes it revise the plan directly.
2. **Manual approval:** the plan card's ▾ menu has a new **Approve in Manual mode** option. The agent carries out the plan but asks before every tool, file edits included. I kept the plain **Approve plan** button as it was (it continues in Accept edits) so existing users don't lose that behavior. It now has a tooltip saying so, to make it clearly different from "Approve and skip permissions".
3. **New setting:** *Settings → Automation → Plan mode → Return to Plan mode after an approved plan*. It's on by default, which keeps today's behavior. Turned off, the chat stays in the mode the plan was approved with for the rest of the conversation. New chats and Restart still start in Plan mode either way.

**Before you rely on it:**
- **Manual approval with the live CLI:** this approval sends the CLI a request to switch into Manual mode at the moment the plan is approved. That's the same way the existing Accept edits and skip-permissions approvals work, but it has only been checked with those two modes and with Auto. Switching to Manual mode the other way, from the permission selector, has been checked. The one thing to confirm with F5 is that after "Approve in Manual mode" the agent really asks before each edit.
- **Translations:** the new text was added to all 19 language files, and I wrote those translations myself.

**Other notes:**
- The README entry, the architecture doc and the unit tests are updated.
- On publish, the Marketplace upload tool failed to sign in on the first try, as it did in earlier releases. The publish script's automatic retry with the other copy of the tool succeeded.
